prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory that Saints names as having a temple announced or being built about 1980.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 20 (about 1980): new temples were announced or under construction in these places. Pin one.
prompts.summary: Around 1980 the Church announced or began building temples in many places outside the United States. Tokyo's temple was dedicated in 1980, and temples followed in Santiago, Mexico City, Apia, Papeete and Nuku'alofa in 1983, Sydney in 1984 and Buenos Aires in 1986. Several new US temples were also underway.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Several new US temples were also underway.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: Listed as Tahiti; Papeete temple followed in 1983.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the Americas with three or more temples, counting announced and under construction.
prompts.text_original: Counting dedicated, under construction and announced temples, pin a country outside the Americas with three or more (as of October 2026).
prompts.note: Counts from the 26 Oct 2026 temple list. Next below the line: Mozambique (2).
prompts.summary: Outside the Americas, the Philippines led with 14 temples dedicated, under construction or announced as of October 2026. Nigeria and Australia had 7 each, Nigeria's being the most in Africa, and the United Kingdom's 4 were the most in Europe.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: 14 in all, the most outside the Americas.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: 7 in all, the most in Africa.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: 4 in all: London, Preston, Birmingham and Edinburgh.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: 3 in all: Frankfurt, Freiberg and Hamburg.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country where Abraham or Jacob lived or travelled.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where Abraham or Jacob lived or travelled
prompts.summary: Abraham's family set out from Ur, traditionally placed in southern Iraq, and stayed for a time at Haran in today's Turkey, where Jacob later served Laban for twenty years (Genesis 11:31; 29-31). Abraham lived at Beersheba and went down to Egypt during a famine. Jacob wrestled at Peniel by the Jabbok in Jordan, and he died in Egypt in the land of Goshen.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Abraham went down to Egypt in a famine, and Jacob died in Goshen (Genesis 12:10; 46-49).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Abraham's family set out from Ur of the Chaldees (Genesis 11:31), traditionally identified with the ancient city of Ur in southern Iraq.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Abraham lived at Beersheba, and Jacob offered sacrifices there (Genesis 21:33; 46:1).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Abraham settled for a time in Haran, and Jacob served Laban there twenty years (Genesis 11:31; 29-31).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Abraham lived at Hebron (Genesis 13:18), in the West Bank.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Jacob wrestled at Peniel by the Jabbok, in Jordan (Genesis 32:22-30).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Abraham chased the captors of Lot to Hobah, north of Damascus (Genesis 14:15).

prompts.display_text: Pin a Pacific country or territory that Saints names as having Church schools in the early 1970s.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 10: in the early 1970s the Church ran schools in these Pacific countries and territories. Pin one.
prompts.summary: In the early 1970s the Church ran schools in several Pacific countries and territories. The best known were the Church College of New Zealand and Liahona High School in Tonga. Others were in Samoa, American Samoa, Tahiti in French Polynesia, and Fiji.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Church College of New Zealand was the best known.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Liahona High School is the best known.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: Called Western Samoa at the time.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Named in the chapter's list of school locations.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that Saints names as the home of an early Seventy from outside the US.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 29 names early Seventies from outside the United States. Pin a home country it names.
prompts.summary: Saints vol. 4 ch. 29 names some early Seventies called from outside the United States. They included Angel Abrea of Argentina, Helio da Rocha Camargo and Helvecio Martins of Brazil, Yoshihiko Kikuchi of Japan, Han In Sang of South Korea and Augusto A. Lim of the Philippines. Others came from Chile, Guatemala and Mexico.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Helio da Rocha Camargo and Helvecio Martins.
